questions.question: How do the IF and IFS functions differ in spreadsheets?
questions.solution_html:
• How do the IF and IFS functions differ in spreadsheets? / [CO2]
  • Ans: The IF and IFS functions are logical functions used in spreadsheets to make decisions
  • based on conditions. However, they differ in their usage and complexity.
  • IF Function
  • The IF function checks a single condition and returns one value if the condition is true and
  • another value if it is false.
  • Syntax: =IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)
  • Example: =IF(A1>=50,"Pass","Fail")
  • To test multiple conditions, nested IF statements are required, which can become
  • lengthy and difficult to understand.
  • IFS Function
  • The IFS function is used to test multiple conditions in a single formula.
  • It returns the value corresponding to the first true condition.
  • Syntax: =IFS(condition1, result1, condition2, result2, )
  • Example: =IFS(A1>=90,"A", A1>=75,"B", A1>=50,"C")
  • It is easier to read and manage compared to nested IF functions.
